Request State Numeric Description Open 1 Not started Work In Progress 2 Fulfillment underway Closed Complete 3 Delivered successfully Closed Incomplete 4 Could not fulfill Closed Skipped 7 Skipped due to approval rejection

docs.title: ServiceNow Work Notes
docs.text: Work notes vs comments, resolution notes, audit trail, and best practices.

docs.title: Work Notes vs Comments (Additional Comments)
docs.text:
ServiceNow has two note fields on every ticket. Understanding the difference prevents accidental information disclosure.

Field Visible To Triggers Notification Use For Work Notes Internal team only Assignee group Technical investigation, internal updates Additional Comments Requester / caller Requester + team Customer-facing communication Resolution Notes Requester Yes (on resolve) Summary of fix for the end user

Never put credentials, internal IP addresses, or sensitive system details in Additional Comments.

docs.title: Adding Work Notes via API
docs.text:
# Add a work note to an incident
curl -u user:token -X PATCH \
  "https://your-instance.service-now.com/api/now/table/incident/SYS_ID" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"work_notes": "Checked error logs on prod-api-01. OOM kill at 14:28 UTC. Restarting service and monitoring."}'

# Add an additional comment (customer-visible)
curl -u user:token -X PATCH \
  "https://your-instance.service-now.com/api/now/table/incident/SYS_ID" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"comments": "We have identified the issue and are working on a fix. Expected resolution within 2 hours."}'

# Add a work note to a change request
curl -u user:token -X PATCH \
  "https://your-instance.service-now.com/api/now/table/change_request/SYS_ID" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"work_notes": "Step 1 complete: database backup verified. Proceeding to step 2."}'

docs.title: Work Note Best Practices
docs.text:
Good work notes make handoffs seamless and post-incident reviews accurate.

# Good work note format
[14:35 UTC] Checked nginx access logs — confirmed 503s starting 14:28 UTC
[14:40 UTC] Correlated with deployment at 14:25 UTC by @jsmith
[14:42 UTC] Rolled back to previous image. Error rate dropping.
[14:50 UTC] Error rate back to baseline 0.1%. Monitoring for 30 min before closing.

Work note checklist: - Include timestamps in UTC - Note who performed each action - Record what was checked, not just what was done - Log any commands run and their output if relevant - Note what was ruled out (helps future investigators)

docs.title: Resolution Notes
docs.text:
Resolution notes are shown to the end user when a ticket is resolved. They should be jargon-free.

# Set resolution notes when closing an incident
curl -u user:token -X PATCH \
  "https://your-instance.service-now.com/api/now/table/incident/SYS_ID" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "state": "6",
    "close_code": "Solved (Permanently)",
    "close_notes": "A misconfigured deployment caused the service to run out of memory. We have rolled back to the previous version and applied a fix. The service has been stable since 15:00 UTC. We will deploy the corrected version during the next maintenance window."
  }'

docs.title: Reading the Audit Trail
docs.text:
The audit trail records every field change with the old value, new value, and who made the change.

# Get audit history for a record
curl -u user:token -G \
  "https://your-instance.service-now.com/api/now/table/sys_audit" \
  --data-urlencode 'sysparm_query=documentkey=SYS_ID' \
  --data-urlencode 'sysparm_fields=fieldname,oldvalue,newvalue,sys_created_by,sys_created_on' \
  | jq '.result[] | {field: .fieldname, from: .oldvalue, to: .newvalue, by: .sys_created_by, at: .sys_created_on}'

# Get journal entries (work notes + comments) for a ticket
curl -u user:token -G \
  "https://your-instance.service-now.com/api/now/table/sys_journal_field" \
  --data-urlencode 'sysparm_query=element_id=SYS_ID' \
  --data-urlencode 'sysparm_fields=name,element,value,sys_created_by,sys_created_on' \
  | jq '.result | sort_by(.sys_created_on)[] | {type: .element, author: .sys_created_by, time: .sys_created_on, note: .value}'

docs.title: Bulk Note Operations
docs.text:
# Add the same work note to multiple incidents (e.g., all P1s during a major outage)
INCIDENTS="INC0001 INC0002 INC0003"
NOTE="Major outage identified — root cause is BGP flap on core-rtr-01. Bridge open in #incident-bridge."

for INC in $INCIDENTS; do
  SYS_ID=$(curl -s -u user:token -G \
    "https://your-instance.service-now.com/api/now/table/incident" \
    --data-urlencode "sysparm_query=number=${INC}" \
    | jq -r '.result[0].sys_id')
  curl -s -u user:token -X PATCH \
    "https://your-instance.service-now.com/api/now/table/incident/${SYS_ID}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"work_notes\": \"${NOTE}\"}"
done
Journal Type element Value Visibility Work notes work_notes Internal only Additional comments comments Customer-visible Resolution notes close_notes Customer (on resolve)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Cross-platform troubleshooting guides for common infrastructure issues.

Authentication FailuresAD, LDAP, Kerberos, and SSO authentication issues — diagnosis and resolution. Backup FailuresVeeam, NetBackup, and Commvault job failures — snapshot errors, proxy issues, and repository problems. DNS ResolutionForward and reverse lookup failures, forwarder issues, and DNS cache problems. High CPUIdentifying CPU-heavy processes on Linux, Windows, and ESXi hosts. Replication FailuresSRDF, SnapMirror, and vSphere Replication failures — link issues, lag, and pair state errors. Storage LatencyHigh I/O latency triage — queue depth, path health, array performance, and contention. VM PerformanceSlow VM diagnosis — CPU ready, memory ballooning, disk latency, and network drops. Network Connectivity Network Connectivity notes, checks, commands, and references.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Authentication failures may occur due to directory service issues, credential problems, certificate errors, or network connectivity problems.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Login failures
  • Account lockouts
  • Expired passwords
  • Kerberos errors

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
Get-EventLog -LogName Security -Newest 20
nltest /dsgetdc:domain
klist

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm user credentials
  2. Verify domain controller availability
  3. Check time synchronization
  4. Review security logs
  5. Reset credentials if required

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Backup failures increase risk of data loss and recovery delays during outages.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Failed backup jobs
  • Missing restore points
  • Repository errors
  • Network timeouts

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
Get-VBRJob
bpdbjobs
qlist job

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify failed job
  2. Review error logs
  3. Validate storage capacity
  4. Confirm network connectivity
  5. Retry backup job

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: DNS failures prevent applications, servers, and services from locating required resources.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Unable to resolve hostname
  • Application connection errors
  • Service startup failures

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
nslookup hostname
dig hostname
ipconfig /flushdns

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm DNS server configuration
  2. Validate network connectivity
  3. Check DNS records
  4. Restart DNS service if required
  5. Test resolution again

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: High CPU utilization can cause performance degradation, latency, and service instability across applications and infrastructure.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• System slow response
  • High load average
  • Application timeouts
  • Monitoring alerts

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
top
htop
ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head
uptime

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify process consuming CPU
  2. Confirm recent changes or deployments
  3. Review logs
  4. Validate resource limits
  5. Restart or scale service if required

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Network connectivity failures prevent systems from communicating across services, storage, and cloud environments.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Unable to reach server
  • Packet loss
  • Application connection failure
  • Timeout errors

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
ping host
traceroute host
ip addr
ip route

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm IP configuration
  2. Validate gateway connectivity
  3. Check routing tables
  4. Review firewall rules
  5. Validate DNS resolution

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Replication failures can impact disaster recovery readiness and data consistency.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Replication lag
  • Synchronization errors
  • Failover readiness warnings

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
snapmirror show
symrdf query
get_group_status

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Verify replication link status
  2. Check network connectivity
  3. Review storage capacity
  4. Confirm configuration settings
  5. Resume replication

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Storage latency impacts application response times, database performance, and VM operations.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Slow disk operations
  • VM performance degradation
  • Database timeouts
  • Increased I/O wait

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
iostat -x 5
vmstat 5
esxtop
symstat

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm latency metrics
  2. Identify impacted volumes or LUNs
  3. Check host connectivity
  4. Review storage alerts
  5. Validate replication or snapshot activity

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Virtual machine performance issues may be caused by CPU contention, memory pressure, storage latency, or network congestion.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Slow application response
  • High CPU ready time
  • Memory swapping
  • Disk latency alerts

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
esxtop
vmstat
top
free -m

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Check CPU and memory utilization
  2. Review storage latency
  3. Confirm network connectivity
  4. Review recent changes
  5. Adjust resource allocation if needed

Operational procedures, health checks, troubleshooting guides, and runbooks for the virtualization platform.

Health Checks Pre- and post-change health checks, daily checks, and validation procedures. Troubleshooting Troubleshooting guides, known issues, and resolution steps across all platforms. Runbooks Step-by-step operational runbooks for common tasks and incidents.

docs.title: Virtualization Health Checks
docs.text:
Reusable health checks for virtualization operations.

Daily Health Check Daily checks across vCenter, ESXi, vSAN, NSX, VxRail, and Aria. Pre-Change Check Checks before maintenance, patching, upgrades, migrations, or config changes. Post-Change Validation Validation after maintenance, upgrades, patching, or configuration changes. Capacity Review Cluster, datastore, vSAN, CPU, memory, and growth review. Alert Review Review active alerts, stale alerts, ownership, and escalation needs. Management Access Check vCenter, ESXi, VxRail Manager, NSX, and Aria access validation.

docs.title: Active Alerts Review
docs.text:
• Review all critical alerts in vCenter — confirm each has an owner or action
  • Review warning alerts — identify any that have been open longer than expected
  • Check for alerts that triggered during a recent maintenance window

docs.title: Aria Operations Alerts
docs.text:
• Review Aria Operations alert dashboard
  • Identify any critical or high-severity alerts
  • Confirm alerts are not suppressed unnecessarily outside maintenance windows

docs.title: Hardware Alerts
docs.text:
• Review iDRAC alerts for all VxRail nodes and other servers
  • Confirm no outstanding disk, memory, NIC, or PSU alerts

docs.title: Backup Alerts
docs.text:
• Review backup platform for failed or missed jobs
  • Confirm all critical VMs and systems have a successful recent backup

docs.title: Repeat Alerts
docs.text:
• Identify alerts that fire repeatedly without resolution
  • Review repeat alerts for tuning or permanent fixes
  • Suppress intentionally only with a documented reason and expiry

docs.title: False Positives and Stale Alerts
docs.text:
• Remove or disable alerts that no longer apply
  • Review alert thresholds — adjust if consistently firing below the meaningful threshold

docs.title: Alert Owner and Next Action
docs.text: For each open critical alert, confirm: - Owner assigned - Next action documented - Escalation path clear if not resolved within SLA

docs.title: Capacity Review
docs.text: Run this check weekly or after any significant workload addition.

docs.title: Cluster CPU and Memory
docs.text:
# Via vCenter PowerCLI
$clusters = Get-Cluster
foreach ($c in $clusters) {
    $hosts = Get-VMHost -Location $c
    $totalCPU = ($hosts | Measure-Object -Property NumCpu -Sum).Sum
    $usedCPU  = ($hosts | Get-Stat -Stat cpu.usage.average -MaxSamples 1 | Measure-Object -Property Value -Average).Average
    Write-Host "$($c.Name): CPU=$($usedCPU.ToString('0.0'))%  Hosts=$($hosts.Count)"
}

Thresholds: - CPU > 70% average across cluster → investigate workload distribution - Memory balloon/swap > 0 on any host → immediate action required

docs.title: Datastore Free Space
docs.text:
Get-Datastore | Select-Object Name, FreeSpaceGB, CapacityGB, @{
    N="Used%"; E={[math]::Round((1-($_.FreeSpaceGB/$_.CapacityGB))*100,1)}
} | Sort-Object "Used%" -Descending | Format-Table -AutoSize

Alert thresholds: - > 75% used: review and plan expansion - > 85% used: immediate action — thin provisioned disks may fail to inflate

docs.title: vSAN Capacity
docs.text:
# On any cluster ESXi host
esxcli vsan storage capacity get
# Review: total capacity, used, free, and "slack" (reserved for rebuild)

# Via vCenter UI: vSAN cluster → Monitor → Capacity
# Check "Used Capacity" — keep below 70% to allow object rebuild headroom

vSAN capacity thresholds: - > 60% used: plan capacity expansion - > 70% used: critical — rebuild operations may fail if a disk fails

docs.title: Snapshot Growth
docs.text:
# Find VMs with large or old snapshots
Get-VM | Get-Snapshot | Where-Object {$_.SizeMB -gt 10240 -or $_.Created -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-7)} |
    Select-Object VM, Name, Created, SizeMB | Sort-Object SizeMB -Descending

Action: snapshots older than 7 days should be reviewed with the VM owner; snapshots > 50 GB should be removed if not actively in use.

docs.title: Thin Provisioning Risk
docs.text:
# Compare provisioned vs. actual used space per datastore
Get-Datastore | Where-Object {$_.Type -eq "VMFS"} | ForEach-Object {
    $ds = $_
    $vms = Get-VM -Datastore $ds
    $provGB = ($vms | Get-HardDisk | Measure-Object -Property CapacityGB -Sum).Sum
    [PSCustomObject]@{
        Datastore = $ds.Name
        CapacityGB = [math]::Round($ds.CapacityGB, 1)
        ProvisionedGB = [math]::Round($provGB, 1)
        OvercommitRatio = [math]::Round($provGB / $ds.CapacityGB, 2)
    }
} | Sort-Object OvercommitRatio -Descending

Alert if overcommit ratio > 2.0 on a datastore approaching 70% usage.

docs.title: Backup Repository Usage
docs.text: Check primary and SOBR capacity tier fill levels — alert operators when performance tier > 80% full: - CommVault: Command Center → Storage → Disk Libraries - Veeam: VBR console → Backup Infrastructure → Repositories - NetBackup: OpsCenter → Reports → Storage Unit Utilization

docs.title: Daily Health Check
docs.text: Morning checks covering all components that can silently degrade overnight. Target: complete in under 15 minutes.

docs.title: 1. vCenter Availability
docs.text:
# Connect and verify vCenter services
Connect-VIServer -Server vcenter.corp.local
Get-View -ViewType ServiceInstance | Select-Object -ExpandProperty ServerClock

# Check vCenter services from appliance shell
service-control --status --all | grep -v stopped

Also check: VCSA VAMI at https://vcenter:5480 — confirm appliance health, disk usage, and certificate expiry.

docs.title: 2. Host Connectivity
docs.text:
# All hosts should be Connected/PoweredOn
Get-VMHost | Select-Object Name, ConnectionState, PowerState, OverallStatus |
    Where-Object { $_.ConnectionState -ne "Connected" -or $_.PowerState -ne "PoweredOn" }

# Any result here = action required

docs.title: 3. Cluster HA / DRS
docs.text:
# Check HA and DRS are enabled
Get-Cluster | Select-Object Name, HAEnabled, DrsEnabled, DrsAutomationLevel

# Check active HA errors
Get-VIEvent -Types Error -MaxSamples 200 |
    Where-Object { $_.FullFormattedMessage -match "HA|DRS" } |
    Select-Object CreatedTime, FullFormattedMessage | Select-Object -First 10

docs.title: 4. Datastore Free Space
docs.text:
# Flag datastores below 20% free
Get-Datastore | Where-Object { ($_.FreeSpaceGB / $_.CapacityGB) -lt 0.20 } |
    Select-Object Name,
        @{N="FreeGB"; E={ [math]::Round($_.FreeSpaceGB,1) }},
        @{N="CapGB";  E={ [math]::Round($_.CapacityGB,1) }},
        @{N="Free%";  E={ [math]::Round($_.FreeSpaceGB/$_.CapacityGB*100,1) }}

docs.title: 5. vSAN Health
docs.text:
# Run on any ESXi host in the vSAN cluster
esxcli vsan health cluster list | grep -v "Green\|healthy"

# Check for resyncing objects
esxcli vsan debug object list | grep -i "Resyncing\|Degraded\|Absent" | wc -l

docs.title: 6. Critical VM Status
docs.text:
# Check VMs with PoweredOff state (expected list should be known)
Get-VM | Where-Object { $_.PowerState -ne "PoweredOn" } |
    Select-Object Name, PowerState, Guest

# Check snapshots older than 3 days
Get-VM | Get-Snapshot | Where-Object { $_.Created -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-3) } |
    Select-Object VM, Name, Created, SizeGB

docs.title: 7. Active Alarms
docs.text:
# All triggered alarms at cluster and higher scope
Get-Folder "Datacenters" | Get-View |
    Select-Object -ExpandProperty TriggeredAlarmState |
    ForEach-Object {
        [PSCustomObject]@{
            Entity = (Get-View $_.Entity).Name
            Alarm  = (Get-View $_.Alarm).Info.Name
            Status = $_.OverallStatus
            Time   = $_.Time
        }
    } | Where-Object { $_.Status -ne "green" }

docs.title: 8. Backup Job Status
docs.text:
# Veeam — check last 24h job results
Get-VBRJob | ForEach-Object {
    $last = Get-VBRRestorePoint -Job $_ | Sort-Object CreationTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
    [PSCustomObject]@{ Job = $_.Name; LastResult = $_.GetLastResult(); LastRun = $_.ScheduleOptions.LatestRunLocal }
} | Where-Object { $_.LastResult -ne "Success" }

docs.title: 9. Identity Source / SSO
docs.text:
# Verify LDAP/AD identity source is reachable
Get-SsoAuthenticationSource | Select-Object Name, Type, Enabled
# Check for recent SSO errors in vCenter events
Get-VIEvent -MaxSamples 100 | Where-Object { $_.FullFormattedMessage -match "SSO\|identity\|LDAP" } |
    Select-Object -First 5 CreatedTime, FullFormattedMessage

docs.title: Daily Check Summary Template
docs.text: Area Status Notes vCenter reachable All hosts connected HA/DRS enabled No datastores < 20% free vSAN health all green No critical VM alarms No stale snapshots All backup jobs succeeded Identity source healthy

docs.title: Management Access Check
docs.text: Run this check weekly to confirm all management endpoints are reachable and access controls are healthy.

docs.title: Connectivity Checks
docs.text:
# Verify DNS resolution for management FQDNs
for fqdn in vcenter.corp.local nsx.corp.local sddc-manager.corp.local aria-ops.corp.local; do
    result=$(nslookup $fqdn 2>/dev/null | grep "Address:" | tail -1)
    echo "$fqdn → $result"
done

# Verify HTTPS reachability
for url in https://vcenter.corp.local https://nsx.corp.local; do
    code=$(curl -sk -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$url")
    echo "$url → HTTP $code"
done

docs.title: vCenter Access
docs.text:
# Verify vCenter login (PowerCLI)
Connect-VIServer -Server vcenter.corp.local -Credential $cred
if ($?) { Write-Host "vCenter: OK" } else { Write-Host "vCenter: FAIL" }

# Check vCenter certificate validity
$cert = [System.Net.ServicePointManager]::ServerCertificateValidationCallback
$expiry = (Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://vcenter.corp.local" -UseBasicParsing).Headers

Checks to perform in vCenter UI: - [ ] vCenter SSO Health: Administration → Single Sign On → Diagnostics → Diagnostic Site Connectivity - [ ] Identity sources: Administration → Single Sign On → Configuration → Identity Sources — all should show Connected - [ ] System health: Administration → Deployments → System Configuration — all services green

docs.title: NSX Manager Access
docs.text:
# Verify NSX Manager cluster health (SSH to NSX Manager)
get cluster status   # Should show: STABLE
get services         # All critical services should show: running

docs.title: SDDC Manager Access (VCF)
docs.text:
# SDDC Manager API health check
curl -k -u admin@local:password https://sddc-manager.corp.local/v1/health-summary | python3 -m json.tool

docs.title: Aria Operations Access
docs.text: Confirm Aria Ops is receiving telemetry: 1. Log in to https://aria-ops.corp.local 2. Environment → Object Browser → confirm vCenter adapter shows Collection State: OK 3. Check last collection time — should be within the last 5 minutes

docs.title: AD/LDAP Identity Source Health
docs.text:
# Test LDAP connectivity (run from a Linux admin host)
ldapsearch -H ldaps://dc1.corp.local:636 -D "cn=svc_vcenter,ou=service_accounts,dc=corp,dc=local" \
    -w '<password>' -b "dc=corp,dc=local" "(sAMAccountName=admin)" sAMAccountName
# Should return at least one result

docs.title: Access Control Review
docs.text:
Run monthly (in addition to weekly connectivity checks):

  • [ ] Review stale user accounts: Administration → Users and Groups — remove leavers
  • [ ] Review service account usage: confirm all service accounts still needed
  • [ ] Verify MFA is enforced for admin console access (via SSO policy or Workspace ONE Access)
  • [ ] Review vCenter role assignments: Administration → Access Control → Roles
  • [ ] Confirm no direct permission grants to individual users (should be via group memberships)
  • [ ] Check break-glass accounts: password still in vault; access log reviewed

docs.title: Failed Login Monitoring
docs.text:
# Check vCenter SSO audit log for failed logins
# /storage/log/vmware/sso/vmware-sts-idmd.log on vCenter appliance
grep "AuthenticationException\|failed.*login\|InvalidCredentials" /var/log/vmware/sso/vmware-sts-idmd.log | tail -20

Alert on > 5 failed logins for any account in a 15-minute window.

docs.title: Post-Change Validation
docs.text: Run these checks after any infrastructure change — maintenance, upgrade, patch, or configuration modification. Document evidence in the change record before closing.

docs.title: Immediate Checks (within 5 minutes of change completion)
docs.text:
# 1. Confirm all hosts are connected to vCenter
Get-VMHost | Where-Object {$_.ConnectionState -ne "Connected"} | Select-Object Name, ConnectionState

# 2. Confirm cluster HA status
Get-Cluster | Select-Object Name, HAEnabled, DrsEnabled, @{N="HA Status"; E={$_.ExtensionData.Summary.OverallStatus}}

# 3. Confirm no VMs in unexpected state
Get-VM | Where-Object {$_.PowerState -ne "PoweredOn" -and $_.PowerState -ne "PoweredOff"} | Select-Object Name, PowerState
# Suspended or unknown states indicate issues

docs.title: Datastore and Storage
docs.text:
# Confirm datastores are accessible (no APD/PDL)
Get-Datastore | Where-Object {$_.State -ne "Available"} | Select-Object Name, State

# vSAN: confirm health is green after change
esxcli vsan health cluster list | grep -v "Green"

docs.title: NSX (if change was NSX-related)
docs.text:
# Verify NSX Manager cluster stability
get cluster status   # All nodes: STABLE

# Verify edge nodes are healthy
get service router
get logical-routers

docs.title: Backup Validation
docs.text:
# Confirm backup jobs are not in failed state after change
# (Veeam)
Get-VBRJob | Where-Object {$_.GetLastState() -eq "Failed"} | Select-Object Name, LastRun

# (CommVault — check via Command Center UI for jobs since change window start)

docs.title: Monitoring Validation
docs.text:
1. Log in to Aria Operations → confirm no new critical or immediate alerts generated by the change
  2. Verify collection is still running: Environment → <cluster name> → Collection State: OK
  3. Check that baseline alerts that existed before the change are not masked by new false positives

docs.title: Application Validation
docs.text: If the change affected production workloads: - Contact the application owner to confirm the application is functioning correctly - Run a basic functional test (login to the app, execute a representative transaction) - Record the application owner's confirmation in the change record

docs.title: Change Record Closure
docs.text:
Before closing the change:

  • [ ] All hosts connected: confirmed
  • [ ] HA/DRS status: verified green
  • [ ] vSAN health: no new alarms
  • [ ] No unexpected VM state changes
  • [ ] Datastores accessible
  • [ ] Backup jobs not broken
  • [ ] Monitoring collecting data
  • [ ] Application owner sign-off (for production changes)
  • [ ] Final component versions captured: 
    Get-VMHost | Select-Object Name, Version, Build | Sort-Object Name
(Get-View ServiceInstance).Content.About.Version   # vCenter version
  • [ ] Change record updated with evidence screenshots or command output

docs.title: Pre-Change Checks
docs.text: Pre-change checks confirm the platform is healthy before maintenance begins. Run these before any host maintenance, upgrade, or configuration change.

docs.title: 1. vCenter and Management Access
docs.text:
# Confirm vCenter is reachable and you can authenticate
Connect-VIServer -Server vcenter.corp.local

# vCenter version and build
$global:DefaultVIServer | Select-Object Name, Version, Build, IsConnected

docs.title: 2. Host Connectivity
docs.text:
# Confirm all hosts are connected and not in maintenance mode
Get-VMHost | Select-Object Name, ConnectionState, PowerState |
    Where-Object { $_.ConnectionState -ne "Connected" -or $_.PowerState -ne "PoweredOn" }

# Any unexpected maintenance mode hosts?
Get-VMHost | Where-Object { $_.ConnectionState -eq "Maintenance" } | Select-Object Name

docs.title: 3. Active Alarms
docs.text:
# Triggered alarms on any host or VM
Get-VMHost | Where-Object { $_.ExtensionData.TriggeredAlarmState.Count -gt 0 } |
    Select-Object Name, @{N="Alarms";E={$_.ExtensionData.TriggeredAlarmState.Count}}

Get-VM | Where-Object { $_.ExtensionData.TriggeredAlarmState.Count -gt 0 } |
    Select-Object Name, @{N="Alarms";E={$_.ExtensionData.TriggeredAlarmState.Count}}

Resolve or acknowledge all critical alarms before proceeding. Warning alarms: document and assess risk.

docs.title: 4. Datastore Free Space
docs.text:
# Datastores below 20% free
Get-Datastore | Where-Object { ($_.FreeSpaceGB / $_.CapacityGB) -lt 0.2 } |
    Select-Object Name, @{N="FreeGB";E={[math]::Round($_.FreeSpaceGB,1)}},
    @{N="UsedPct";E={[math]::Round((1-$_.FreeSpaceGB/$_.CapacityGB)*100,1)}}

docs.title: 5. Snapshot Audit
docs.text:
# Any snapshots older than 24h or larger than 10 GB
Get-VM | Get-Snapshot |
    Where-Object { $_.Created -lt (Get-Date).AddHours(-24) -or $_.SizeGB -gt 10 } |
    Select-Object @{N="VM";E={$_.VM.Name}}, Name, Created,
    @{N="SizeGB";E={[math]::Round($_.SizeGB,2)}}

docs.title: 6. vSAN Health
docs.text:
# Run on each ESXi host in vSAN cluster
esxcli vsan health summary get
esxcli vsan debug resync list   # should be empty before maintenance
esxcli vsan debug object list | grep -v healthy   # should return nothing

docs.title: 7. Storage Paths
docs.text:
# Any dead paths?
esxcli storage core path list | grep "State: dead"

# Count of active paths (should match expected multipath config)
esxcli storage core path list | grep -c "State: active"

docs.title: 8. NTP and DNS
docs.text:
# ESXi host time is synchronised
esxcli system ntp get

# Forward and reverse DNS resolves correctly
nslookup $(hostname)
nslookup vcenter.corp.local

docs.title: 9. Cluster HA and DRS
docs.text:
# HA and DRS state
Get-Cluster | Select-Object Name, HAEnabled, DrsEnabled, DrsAutomationLevel

# Any DRS faults or admission control warnings
Get-Cluster | Select-Object Name,
    @{N="HAStatus";E={$_.ExtensionData.Summary.OverallStatus}}

docs.title: 10. Backup Status
docs.text: Confirm that the most recent backup completed successfully before making changes. A failed backup combined with a botched change = data at risk.

docs.title: 11. Version Capture
docs.text:
# Capture current versions before upgrade
Get-VMHost | Select-Object Name, Version, Build | Export-Csv -Path pre_change_versions.csv -NoTypeInformation
$global:DefaultVIServer | Select-Object Name, Version, Build

docs.title: 12. Rollback Plan Confirmed
docs.text:
Before proceeding, document and confirm:

  • [ ] Rollback procedure is documented
  • [ ] Maintenance window approval received
  • [ ] Change record number noted
  • [ ] Escalation contact available during window
  • [ ] Time-boxed: if task not complete by X, abort and revert

docs.title: Pre-Change Summary Table
docs.text: Check Expected Status vCenter accessible Connected All hosts Connected No Maintenance Active critical alarms Zero Datastore free space > 20% Snapshots > 24h Zero vSAN health All GREEN vSAN resync Not running Dead storage paths Zero NTP synchronised Yes Backup complete Yes

docs.title: Virtualization Runbooks
docs.text:
Practical runbooks for incidents, maintenance, lifecycle work, validation, evidence collection, and RCA follow-up.

Incident Response Use this during virtualization incidents where VMs, hosts, clusters, datastores, networking, or management tools are impacted. Maintenance Window Runbook Use this for planned work across VMware, VxRail, NSX, Aria, hosts, clusters, or related services. Host Evacuation Runbook Use this before host maintenance, patching, hardware work, or lifecycle activity. VM Snapshot Cleanup Runbook Use this to find and clean up old or risky VM snapshots. VM Lifecycle Runbook Use this for VM build, change, ownership, review, retirement, and cleanup. Storage Path Validation Use this after SAN changes, storage maintenance, host work, or datastore alerts. Network Validation Use this after network changes, VLAN changes, host work, NSX changes, or VM connectivity issues. Certificate Renewal Planning Use this before vCenter, NSX, VxRail, Aria, or related certificate renewals. Evidence Collection Use this before vendor escalation, RCA work, or major incident review. RCA Template Use this after a virtualization incident or recurring problem. Backup Failure Backup Failure notes, checks, commands, and references. vCenter Outage vCenter Outage notes, checks, commands, and references.

docs.title: Identify Failed VMs
docs.text:
• Review the backup platform for failed or missed backup jobs
  • Note the VM name, backup job name, error message, and failure time

docs.title: Review the Error Message
docs.text: Common backup errors: - Snapshot creation failure - Snapshot consolidation warning - Datastore out of space - Network or proxy connectivity failure - vCenter API error

docs.title: Check VM Snapshot State
docs.text:
• In vCenter: right-click the VM → Snapshots → Manage Snapshots
  • Confirm no stale backup snapshots are present
  • If consolidation is needed: right-click VM → Snapshots → Consolidate

docs.title: Check Datastore Free Space
docs.text:
• Confirm the datastore hosting the VM has sufficient free space
  • Free space less than 10% can block snapshot creation

docs.title: Check Backup Proxy Health
docs.text:
• Confirm the backup proxy VM is powered on and reachable
  • Review proxy logs in the backup platform

docs.title: Check Backup Repository
docs.text:
• Confirm the backup repository has sufficient free space
  • Confirm the repository is accessible from the proxy

docs.title: Check vCenter Permissions
docs.text:
• Confirm the backup service account has the required vCenter permissions
  • Review vCenter roles and recent permission changes

docs.title: Retry the Backup
docs.text:
• If the root cause is resolved, manually retry the backup job
  • Monitor the retry and confirm it completes successfully

docs.title: Escalate Recurring Failures
docs.text:
• If the same VM fails repeatedly, escalate to the backup platform team
  • Open a support case with the backup vendor if needed

docs.title: Document Resolution
docs.text:
• Update the backup platform job notes with the root cause and fix
  • Update the incident ticket with findings and resolution

docs.title: Identify the Expiring Certificate
docs.text:
• Review certificate inventory
  • Confirm the certificate type: Machine SSL, STS, solution user, or integration endpoint
  • Note the affected product and expiration date

docs.title: Confirm Affected Products
docs.text:
• List all products that trust or use this certificate
  • Confirm which integrations may be disrupted during replacement

docs.title: Capture Current Certificate Details
docs.text:
• Subject, SAN, issuer, expiration date
  • Screenshot from VAMI or vSphere Client as pre-change evidence

docs.title: Confirm Backup Exists
docs.text:
• Confirm vCenter file-based backup is current
  • Confirm product backup for Aria or NSX if their certificate is being replaced

docs.title: Schedule Maintenance Window
docs.text:
• Plan replacement outside peak hours
  • Allow time for service restarts and integration validation

docs.title: Replace the Certificate
docs.text:
• Follow the correct replacement method for the certificate type
  • For VMCA-issued certs: use vSphere Client or VAMI
  • For custom CA certs: generate CSR, submit to CA, import signed cert

docs.title: Restart Required Services
docs.text:
service-control --restart --all

Only restart services after confirming the new certificate is applied.

docs.title: Validate Integrations
docs.text:
• vCenter browser access — no certificate warning
  • SSO login for local and AD accounts
  • Aria, NSX, backup, and monitoring integrations confirmed

docs.title: Document Final Expiration Date
docs.text:
• Update the certificate inventory with the new expiration date
  • Set a review reminder 60 days before the new expiration

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Use this before vendor escalation, RCA work, or major incident review.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm issue scope.
  • Confirm affected objects.
  • Confirm timestamps.
  • Confirm recent changes.
  • Confirm ticket or case number if available.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Capture screenshots of alarms.
  2. Export recent tasks and events.
  3. Capture affected object names.
  4. Capture timestamps and timezone.
  5. Collect support bundles if needed.
  6. Record commands already run.
  7. Record impact and current status.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Evidence is complete enough for handoff.
  • Timeline is clear.
  • Affected systems are listed.
  • Next owner has what they need.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Stop the change if impact increases.
  • Return settings to the last known good state where possible.
  • Reconnect affected systems if disconnected.
  • Escalate with logs, timestamps, screenshots, and task IDs.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Keep this page updated with local commands, screenshots, system names, and known environment quirks.

docs.title: Confirm Impact
docs.text:
• Identify the affected host
  • Check vCenter — is the host Disconnected, Not Responding, or in Error?
  • Identify which VMs were running on the host
  • Confirm HA status — have VMs been restarted on other hosts?

docs.title: Check Power State
docs.text:
• Log into iDRAC and confirm power state
  • If powered off unexpectedly, check power supply health and power events in iDRAC

docs.title: Check Management Network
docs.text:
• Ping the host management IP
  • Check DNS forward and reverse lookup for the hostname
  • Confirm the management switch port is active

docs.title: Check Hardware Management Interface
docs.text:
• Log into iDRAC and review hardware health
  • Check for disk, memory, NIC, or PSU failures
  • Review Lifecycle Controller logs for recent hardware events

docs.title: Review vCenter Alarms
docs.text:
• Confirm which alarms are active on the host
  • Check related cluster and datastore alarms

docs.title: Identify Affected VMs
docs.text:
• Confirm which VMs were running on the failed host
  • Verify HA has restarted critical VMs on other hosts
  • Check application owners for any workloads that did not restart

docs.title: Logs to Collect
docs.text:
• iDRAC hardware logs and screenshots
  • vCenter events from the time of the failure
  • ESXi host logs if accessible via SSH or support bundle
  • Aria Operations alerts at the time of failure

docs.title: Engage Hardware Support
docs.text:
• Open a Dell support case if hardware failure is confirmed
  • Provide iDRAC logs, hardware event screenshots, and host serial number

docs.title: Validate Cluster Health After Recovery
docs.text:
• Confirm all remaining hosts are Connected
  • Confirm HA and DRS are active
  • Confirm vSAN object health is green if vSAN is used
  • Confirm VMs are running on healthy hosts
  • Update the change or incident ticket with findings

docs.title: Incident Response Runbook
docs.text: Use this when there is an active VMware platform issue.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Confirm the issue scope
  2. Identify impacted systems
  3. Check vCenter availability
  4. Check host and cluster health
  5. Review active alarms
  6. Check recent tasks and events
  7. Check datastore and vSAN health
  8. Check network health
  9. Check hardware alerts
  10. Review logs
  11. Escalate if needed
  12. Document findings
  13. Confirm recovery
  14. Communicate status
  15. Complete RCA if required

docs.title: Evidence to Capture
docs.text:
• Date and time of issue
  • Impacted VMs, hosts, clusters, or datastores
  • Screenshots of alarms
  • Recent vCenter events
  • Logs from vCenter or ESXi
  • Support bundles if needed
  • Timeline of actions taken
  • Validation after recovery

docs.title: Maintenance Window Runbook
docs.text: Use this for planned VMware work.

docs.title: Before Maintenance
docs.text:
• Review change ticket
  • Confirm maintenance window
  • Notify stakeholders
  • Confirm backups
  • Confirm current health
  • Confirm rollback plan
  • Capture versions
  • Confirm access
  • Confirm vendor support if needed

docs.title: During Maintenance
docs.text:
• Start maintenance window
  • Place host in maintenance mode if required
  • Perform approved work
  • Monitor cluster and workload health
  • Capture screenshots or logs
  • Escalate if unexpected issues occur

docs.title: After Maintenance
docs.text:
• Validate cluster health
  • Confirm VMs are running
  • Confirm datastores are accessible
  • Confirm monitoring is clean
  • Confirm backups still work
  • Update ticket with results
  • Send completion notice

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Use this after network changes, VLAN changes, host work, NSX changes, or VM connectivity issues.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm affected VLANs or segments.
  • Confirm port groups or NSX segments.
  • Confirm uplink status.
  • Confirm recent switch or firewall changes.
  • Confirm affected VM scope.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Check VM network assignment.
  2. Check port group or segment configuration.
  3. Check host uplinks.
  4. Check VLAN or overlay configuration.
  5. Check gateway reachability.
  6. Check NSX edge and routing if used.
  7. Test from affected and unaffected VMs.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• VM connectivity works.
  • Uplinks are healthy.
  • VLAN or segment config is correct.
  • Routing is working.
  • No new network alarms.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Stop the change if impact increases.
  • Return settings to the last known good state where possible.
  • Reconnect affected systems if disconnected.
  • Escalate with logs, timestamps, screenshots, and task IDs.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Keep this page updated with local commands, screenshots, system names, and known environment quirks.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Brief description of what happened.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text: Systems, users, applications, or services affected.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: Time Event HH:MM Issue detected HH:MM Investigation started HH:MM Cause identified HH:MM Fix applied HH:MM Service restored

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text: Explain the actual cause of the issue.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: Explain what was done to fix it.

docs.title: Prevention
docs.text: List steps to reduce the chance of the issue happening again.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Attach logs, screenshots, events, support case numbers, and validation results.

docs.title: Confirm vSAN Health State
docs.text:
• Open vCenter → Cluster → vSAN → Skyline Health
  • Identify which health checks are failing
  • Open Virtual Objects view and filter by Degraded, Non-compliant, or Absent

docs.title: Identify Affected Objects
docs.text:
• Note the VM name, object type, and storage policy for each affected object
  • Check if the VM is still running or if it has failed

docs.title: Check Failed Disks
docs.text:
• Review Skyline Health → Physical Disk section
  • Check iDRAC for disk health on all VxRail nodes

docs.title: Check Host Availability
docs.text:
• Confirm all hosts are Connected in vCenter
  • Check if any host is in maintenance mode unexpectedly

docs.title: Check Resync Status
docs.text:
esxcli vsan debug resync summary get

Active resync is expected after a host returns from maintenance — wait for it to complete before taking further action.

docs.title: Check Capacity
docs.text:
• Confirm vSAN usable capacity is within safe limits
  • If capacity is the cause of non-compliance, expansion may be needed

docs.title: Review Storage Policy
docs.text:
• Confirm the storage policy assigned to affected objects is achievable with current cluster state
  • If FTT=1 and only one host or disk is available, the policy cannot be met

docs.title: Avoid Unsafe Actions
docs.text:
• Do not take additional hosts into maintenance mode while objects are degraded
  • Do not delete VMs or disks without VMware support guidance

docs.title: Engage VMware Support
docs.text:
• Collect a vSAN support bundle if objects remain degraded after the expected recovery period
  • Open a VMware support case and provide the bundle, timeline, and Skyline Health screenshots

docs.title: Validate Object Compliance After Recovery
docs.text:
• Return to Virtual Objects view and confirm all objects are Healthy
  • Run Skyline Health and confirm no remaining failures

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Use this after SAN changes, storage maintenance, host work, or datastore alerts.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm affected hosts and datastores.
  • Confirm storage array status.
  • Confirm SAN zoning or masking changes.
  • Confirm no active datastore outage.
  • Confirm maintenance window if changes are planned.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Check datastore visibility.
  2. Check host storage adapters.
  3. Check path count and path state.
  4. Check multipathing policy.
  5. Review storage latency.
  6. Confirm VMs can access datastores.
  7. Compare against expected path design.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Expected paths are visible.
  • No dead paths remain unless expected.
  • Datastores are mounted.
  • Latency is normal.
  • No new storage alarms.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Stop the change if impact increases.
  • Return settings to the last known good state where possible.
  • Reconnect affected systems if disconnected.
  • Escalate with logs, timestamps, screenshots, and task IDs.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Keep this page updated with local commands, screenshots, system names, and known environment quirks.

docs.title: Confirm Outage Scope
docs.text:
• Can you access the vSphere Client?
  • Can you ping the vCenter FQDN and IP?
  • Are ESXi hosts still visible and running workloads independently?

docs.title: Check VCSA VM Power State
docs.text:
• Confirm the VCSA VM is powered on in vCenter (if a secondary vCenter is available)
  • Or verify via iDRAC/IPMI if the VCSA is running on a known host

docs.title: Check VCSA Appliance Management
docs.text:
• Access https://<vcenter>:5480
  • Review service health, disk partitions, and CPU/memory

docs.title: Check DNS and Network Reachability
docs.text:
ping <vcenter-ip>
nslookup <vcenter-fqdn>

docs.title: Check Service Status
docs.text:
# SSH to vCenter appliance
service-control --status

docs.title: Check Disk Partitions
docs.text:
df -h

Partitions that commonly cause failures when full: - /storage/log - /storage/db

docs.title: Review Recent Changes
docs.text:
• Was a certificate recently replaced?
  • Was a patch or upgrade recently applied?
  • Was a snapshot taken or deleted on the VCSA VM?

docs.title: Restore from Backup if Required
docs.text:
• Use the vCenter file-based backup (VAMI → Backup)
  • Confirm the backup date and restore target
  • Follow VMware restore documentation

docs.title: Validate Services After Recovery
docs.text:
• Confirm all services are running: service-control --status
  • Confirm vSphere Client is accessible
  • Confirm all hosts are reconnecting
  • Confirm Aria and other integrations are working

docs.title: Communicate Impact
docs.text:
• Notify stakeholders of the outage and recovery status
  • Note that ESXi hosts and VMs continue running without vCenter
  • Update the incident ticket with timeline and resolution

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Use this for VM build, change, ownership, review, retirement, and cleanup.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm VM owner.
  • Confirm business purpose.
  • Confirm sizing.
  • Confirm backup policy.
  • Confirm monitoring.
  • Confirm network and security requirements.
  • Confirm naming standard.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Validate request details.
  2. Build or update VM.
  3. Apply naming and tagging standards.
  4. Confirm backup and monitoring.
  5. Validate access and connectivity.
  6. Record owner and lifecycle notes.
  7. Review unused VMs regularly.
  8. Decommission cleanly when approved.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• VM has owner.
  • VM follows naming standard.
  • Backup is assigned.
  • Monitoring is active.
  • Tags or inventory notes are current.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Stop the change if impact increases.
  • Return settings to the last known good state where possible.
  • Reconnect affected systems if disconnected.
  • Escalate with logs, timestamps, screenshots, and task IDs.
